required_fixes_from_last_judge.what: S1 (major). In Install step 5, make the trigger the first stop condition. Under "Triggered via" it must read "push", and the run's ref label must be the tag v2.1.0. "pull request", any other trigger, or a branch name means stop, even when the commit matches. Replace the sentence "A run of the tagged commit can only come from main's reviewed release.yml" with the true one: the 40-character check rules out runs of other commits, and together with "push of the tag" it shows the run used the tagged commit's release.yml. A pull-request run can show the tagged commit while running another branch's workflow file. Qualify the "more than one Release run" tripwire: anyone with Write access can delete a run, so seeing only one run proves nothing. Keep it only as an extra reason to stop. Docs only.
required_fixes_from_last_judge.why: The sentence is false. A pull_request run takes its workflow file from refs/pull/N/merge, so the file can come from any base branch a Write member creates. The run page still shows and links the PR head commit, which can be the tagged commit, under Release / .github/workflows/release.yml with run-name v2.1.0. Same-repo PR tokens can request packages: write. The doc tells IT the commit match proves the run is genuine. An IT person who trusts that and copies the digest from such a run puts unreviewed code on the production server, which holds the live .env.

So every upgrade, rollback and restore, whichever guide it is in, must set HUB_IMAGE to the matching version before the hub starts. last_judge_summary:
Not done yet. Two major objections stand, though every "done when" item is met. The full suite passes (156 OK). Both workflows parse, pin every action to a SHA and keep least-privilege permissions. The release steps match the Dockerfile's last stage (migrate, then gunicorn on 8000) and the compose override (app and scheduler use HUB_IMAGE with build reset). Settings read DB_HOST/DB_NAME/DB_USER, the same form the workflows and compose use. All 11 migrations are reviewed.

Upheld:
- S1 (major): RELEASES.md Install step 5 wrongly says a run of the tagged commit can only come from main's release.yml. A pull_request run shows the PR head commit but runs another branch's workflow file, and Write members can delete runs. Fix: make "Triggered via push" with the tag as its ref a stop condition, replace the false sentence, and qualify the one-run tripwire.
- C1 (major): with the release lines on, only HUB_IMAGE sets the version. team/handover's RUNBOOK (upgrade, rollback, monthly build) and team/rollout's ADMIN-GUIDE (update, restore with git checkout plus --build) silently break. Their files differ from this branch's, so no merge conflict will flag them, and rollout's Restore would reapply the new release's migrations to restored data. Fix: say this in RELEASES.md and .env.example, stop claiming other guides already point here, and add both teams to the hand-offs.
- Minor, cheap to do in the same round: S2 (a format check that HUB_IMAGE carries @sha256), adding push_privacy and show_presence to the hub 0004 row, and C2 (report 15-version-releases-clearly, not 15-automate-release-notes).

Still open and minor: no image scan (08-scan-container-images), unsigned images (10-sign-and-verify-images, 07-sign-commits-and-releases), S4 (fails safe), the NUL-byte 500 on Postgres (handed to qa/redteam), merge order with reliability and hardening, and the Netlify blueprint update, which this team may not do.

10-automate-build-test-and-deploy and 10-keep-one-click-rollback move forward but aren't counted until C1 and S1 land. Checked only by reading: GitHub run-page and ruleset behaviour, GHCR, Compose 2.24 and Postgres 17.

last_build.summary: Round 3 is done: all five of the judge's required fixes are in, and none are disputed. The fixes are in docs/operations/RELEASES.md and CHANGELOG.md, plus comment-only edits to both workflows. S1/C1: in Install step 5, IT now compares the run's full 40-character commit id with `git rev-parse "refs/tags/v2.1.0^{commit}"`, and stops if they differ or if more than one Release run carries the version. Set up step 1 adds a branch ruleset `Version names` (v*, Restrict creations, Repository admin as the only bypass). S2/C2: "adds only" now means the previous version still shows and protects every row the new version wrote. Two cases now need the backup to roll back: new columns or tables that hide something or limit who sees it, and moving data to a new place without writing both. This is in the version table, both rollback paragraphs, the Expand rules, the Renaming bullet, the migration review (hub 0002 deleted_at; hub 0004 is_private, is_draft, audiences, share_email) and the CHANGELOG legend. S3: at least one release each month before the second-Wednesday patching (a version-and-changelog-only patch if nothing merged), and a same-day patch for urgent Debian or Python fixes. C5: a Postgres version change always needs the backup, whatever its Database changes line says. C4: release.yml's header now says the postgres:17 service and the Dockerfile base are named by tag. postgres.yml's header no longer oversells what it catches. Both workflows parse as YAML, all actions are SHA-pinned and the permissions are unchanged. The full suite passes. I published team/pipeline and removed the worktree. I did not touch Netlify or the board, so getting this onto the Netlify blueprint is still open. The build steps also forbade it.
open_items: Not done here: putting this on the Netlify blueprint board (https://one-supreme-blueprint.netlify.app), which the relayed user request asks for. The computed task forbade touching Netlify or the board, so the orchestrator or app-blueprint step has to do it.

Hand-off to team/foundations (GITHUB-SETUP.md section 9). Keep its monthly release rule, but make it 'every month, even with nothing merged', to match RELEASES.md. Its urgent path 'ask IT to rebuild the release already installed' (`docker compose build --pull --no-cache`) stops rebuilding the hub once docker-compose.release.yml is on, so it must become 'cut a patch release the same day'. Also reconcile at merge: v2.0/v2.1 versus v2.0.0 tags, RELEASE-NOTES.md versus CHANGELOG.md, and the duplicate tag ruleset ('Protect releases'; RELEASES.md says to skip ours if it exists). Foundations' digest-pinned FROM and apt-get upgrade in the Dockerfile are what make a version-only monthly patch bring in Debian fixes. On this branch's Dockerfile, a fresh build with --pull gets the newest python:3.12-slim and ffmpeg.

Merge order (judge's C3 note): merge with or after team/reliability, whose backup and restore services and BACKUPS.md the rollback steps point to. README.md conflicts with team/hardening, team/reliability and team/handover; 'Docker Compose 2.24 or newer' must survive the merge. Hardening's migrate service must join docker-compose.release.yml (image: ${HUB_IMAGE}, build: !reset null).

Still open from round 1, all minor: C9-C14. There is no container image scan (08-scan-container-images). Images are unsigned (10-sign-and-verify-images, 07-sign-commits-and-releases). S4 (a pre-pushed tag or re-run blocks a release) stays open; the judge says it fails safe.
For team/qa or team/redteam: psycopg 3 rejects NUL bytes, so `?q=%00` on the search views returns a 500 on Postgres only.

Checked only by reading: neither workflow has run on GitHub. GitHub ruleset behaviour (the v* branch pattern), the commit link's address on the run page, and GHCR, Docker, Compose 2.24 and Postgres 17 behaviour were not exercised. The postgres:17 service image is still not pinned by digest; I softened the comment instead, which the judge allowed as an alternative.
